title: PRJ-1 — Docs Viewer Local Folder Links Delivery
summary: deliver dlf-local body links with base-relative targets, confined Manage activation, and inert public projection
content_html:
PRJ-1 — Docs Viewer Local Folder Links Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as PRJ-1, the first delivery under Projects.

This delivery implements the reusable contract in Local File And Folder Links Concept. It establishes body-link authoring, rendering, public projection, and confined activation before Project metadata assigns any semantic meaning to a target.

Complete Outcome

In a Manage Source editor, an author can paste a local file: URL, absolute path, or shell-backslash-escaped absolute path contained below $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/. Docs Viewer strips that configured root and inserts one marked Markdown link whose payload is a normalized relative path:

[3 symbols](dlf-local:projects/3%20symbols)

Manage can open an existing target through the local service. A public projection retains safe label text but removes the local-link behaviour and target.

The link remains prose. It does not create Project metadata, enter a manifest, or identify a folder to Studio.

Fixed Contract

  • The canonical target is a normalized POSIX path relative to $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/; the configured root is never stored.
  • Body source uses dlf-local:<percent-encoded-relative-target> so it cannot be confused with an ordinary relative web link.
  • The focused editor reads only the current browser paste event. It does not monitor or poll the clipboard.
  • One complete recognized in-root path is converted. Outside-root, mixed, multiline, ambiguous, and code-context input is pasted normally.
  • Input is inert data: no shell evaluation, variable or home expansion, command substitution, or non-file: input scheme.
  • Storage may describe a prospective missing target. Activation requires an existing target and repeats decoding, traversal, and symlink-aware containment checks server-side.
  • Local Manage intercepts the rendered link and sends only the exact relative target to the management service.
  • Public projection removes the marker and target, retaining a safe label as inert text or using the agreed placeholder.
  • Ordinary relative and external links retain their current rendering and navigation behaviour.
  • PRJ-1 adds no Semantic Token, registry, Project metadata, or general-purpose public secret/path redactor.

Delivery Discipline

PRJ-1 should be a small integration over existing seams: one compact normalizer/validator, one narrow local-open endpoint, a focused-editor paste handler, a dlf-local: rendering/public-projection rule, and focused tests. It must not grow a registry, filesystem browser, metadata system, generic secret scanner, platform framework, or Project-specific workflow.

PRJ-1.0 must record the exact proposed files, reused owners, and a rough split of production and test diff size before implementation. Hundreds of new production-code lines are a pause-and-explain signal; thousands mean the delivery has escaped its design and must be split or simplified. Line count is a review trigger rather than a target to game: duplicated or compressed code does not make an oversized design acceptable.

Rough Delivery Steps

PRJ-1.0 — Freeze Input And Link Contract

  • [ ] Trace current Markdown insertion/rendering, public projection, Source editor paste handling, and local management-service boundaries.
  • [ ] Freeze accepted input, excluded editor contexts, relative-path encoding, label derivation, confirmation/Undo, errors, and exact activation payload.
  • [ ] Freeze Manage anchor behaviour, inert public output and placeholder, server revalidation, and ordinary-link preservation.
  • [ ] Record the exact file list, reused seams, rough production/test diff estimate, and any proposed expansion before implementation approval.

Checkpoint: representative Finder, terminal, encoded URL, missing-target, outside-root, contained non-projects/, manually authored dlf-local:, public, and malicious inputs have reviewed expected results.

PRJ-1.1 — Implement Normalization And Confined Open

  • [ ] Add the shared parser/normalizer and focused relative-target containment tests.
  • [ ] Add the local opener over one exact validated relative target.
  • [ ] Return contained missing, invalid, outside-root, and unsupported-platform states without invoking Finder.

PRJ-1.2 — Integrate Authoring And Rendering

  • [ ] Add paste/insert preview to the appropriate Source editing control.
  • [ ] Render dlf-local: body links as clickable local links in Manage and route clicks through the exact validated opener.
  • [ ] Project the same link as safe inert public output with no marker, target, endpoint, control, or activation capability.
  • [ ] Preserve normal relative and external-link behaviour.

PRJ-1.3 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused parser, containment, route/service, renderer, editor, public projection, ordinary-link regression, lint, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Manually test paths with spaces, ~ characters, percent encoding, backslash escaping, missing folders, and long iCloud paths.
  • [ ] Record shipped link syntax and activation behavior in the durable Source Editor and Management Services owners.

Not In Scope

  • folder_path front matter or manifest projection;
  • Projects sub-scope customization or seeding;
  • Project State or Studio Work reads;
  • Resolver Tokens;
  • arbitrary filesystem browsing;
  • content-wide public private-path transformation; or
  • a final public-payload private-path verifier.

Completion Evidence

  • Accepted path forms normalize deterministically and unsafe forms fail closed.
  • Existing allowed folders open through one exact server-validated action.
  • Missing and prospective links remain readable without activating a fallback.
  • Public output retains agreed safe labels or placeholders while containing no dlf-local: target, opener control, or management-service dependency.
  • Real Source-editor and rendered-document review covers representative iCloud folder paths in dotlineform.
